theoryContent:
Pascal's Principle:
A pressure change applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of the fluid and the walls of the vessel. In a hydraulic press, force multiplication matches the area ratio: F₂/F₁ = A₂/A₁ giving mechanical advantage. In ideal conditions work is conserved (F₁d₁ = F₂d₂).

Bernoulli's Equation & Venturi Effect:
For laminar, steady, incompressible horizontal flow, the sum of static pressure and dynamic pressure is constant: P + ½ρv² = constant.
By continuity (A₁v₁ = A₂v₂), narrowing the cross-section forces the velocity to increase, which dramatically decreases static pressure in the throat. In real mode, viscous boundary friction causes head loss.
apparatusMode_desc: Select between Venturi Tube Flow (Bernoulli) or Hydraulic Lift (Pascal)
fluidType_desc: Fluid type to examine density effects on static and dynamic pressures
inletVelocity_desc: Fluid velocity entering the wide pipe section
constrictionRatio_desc: Diameter ratio between narrow throat and inlet
inputForce_desc: Force applied on the primary input piston
pistonAreaRatio_desc: Area ratio of output to input piston (Ideal mechanical advantage)
continuityExpl: Cross-sectional area times velocity remains constant along streamline (A₁v₁ = A₂v₂)
bernoulliExpl: Static fluid pressure drops in constriction as kinetic energy increases
pascalExpl: Pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished in all directions
